mainTopic: How deep a deadly pit must be, and who is liable when two people dig or own one pit
overview: The amud opens by finishing a debate between רבא and רב נחמן about whether a fall into a pit under ten טפחים can kill. רב נחמן first explains that a small pit has enough הבל to injure but not to kill. רבא then challenges him from the height of the בית הסקילה, which the גמרא explains as giving a merciful death (מיתה יפה). רבא's second challenge comes from the ten טפחים of מעקה. After a back-and-forth about what counts as a בית, the גמרא gives רב נחמן's real reason: an ox's belly adds four טפחים, so it really falls ten. A new משנה then rules that when two partners each pass their pit without covering it, the second is liable. The גמרא asks how two people can share a pit, and רבי יוחנן answers that they removed the last clump together. The גמרא then explains the מחלוקת between רבי and the רבנן about one digger finishing another's pit, and the sources for each side. The amud ends with two ברייתות that seem to contradict each other about several people working on one pit; the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: A small pit lacks the deadly heat
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers רבא: a pit under ten טפחים is exempt for death because it has no killing הבל, not because the impact cannot kill.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the owner is exempt because there is no deadly air and heat in it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא's earlier question. The owner is exempt because a small pit has no killing הבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumed the owner is exempt because a short fall cannot kill. רב נחמן says no: the impact can kill, which is why the ox in the water channel may be a טרפה. The Torah's liability for a pit death depends on the pit's הבל, and a small pit does not have enough of it to kill.

keyTerms.meaning: The heat and stuffy air at the bottom of a pit
It does not have in it

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying the fall is harmless. He agrees the fall itself can kill. He is only explaining why the pit's owner is not liable for the death.

phrases.english: No, it is because there are no fumes in it.
phrases.notes: רב נחמן is answering the question from the end of the last page: why is a pit under ten טפחים exempt if the animal dies?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from the previous page.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the reason behind the משנה's exemption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The exemption means a fall of less than ten טפחים cannot kill.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fall can kill, but a pit that small has no deadly הבל, and liability for a death depends on the הבל.

steps.title: Then why is the owner liable for injury?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks: if the small pit has no הבל, why does the משנה make the owner liable when the animal is injured?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the משנה say that if the animal was injured he is liable? There is no heat in it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב נחמן's answer. The משנה says the owner pays for injuries in a small pit, but according to רב נחמן that pit has no הבל at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a pit's harm comes from its הבל, and a small pit has none, it should not be liable for anything. Yet the משנה says it is liable for injury. So רבא argues that רב נחמן's explanation seems to break the second half of the משנה.

phrases.english: If so, why is it taught: if it was injured in it, he is liable?
But there are no fumes in it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that a small pit has no הבל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No הבל should mean no liability at all, yet the משנה makes the owner liable for injury.

steps.title: Enough heat to injure, not to kill
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that a small pit has too little הבל to kill but enough to injure.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There is not enough heat to kill, but there is enough heat to injure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן clarifies his answer. A small pit has some הבל, just not enough to kill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amount of הבל matters. A pit under ten טפחים has enough to injure, so the owner is liable for injury. It does not have enough to kill, so he is exempt for death. This fits both halves of the משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: At this stage, רב נחמן says a pit under ten טפחים has enough הבל to injure but not enough to kill, while the impact of the fall can kill. Step 15 later changes his reasoning: the ox really falls ten טפחים.

phrases.english: He said to him: There are no fumes for death,
but there are fumes for injuries.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A small pit has no הבל at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: It has a small amount of הבל: enough to injure, not enough to kill.

steps.title: Challenge from the height of the stoning platform
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that if a fall of under ten טפחים can kill, the בית הסקילה would not need to be three people's height.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged him: The stoning platform was two people high, and a ברייתא adds that with the condemned person's own height, that makes three. If a fall of less than ten טפחים can kill, why is all this height needed?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a new challenge from the laws of סקילה (stoning). The platform the condemned person was pushed from was very high.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן holds that the impact of even a short fall can kill. If so, a low platform would be enough to carry out the death penalty. The fact that the court used a total height of three people suggests a short fall cannot kill.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him from a written source

phrases.english: He raised an objection: The stoning platform
phrases.notes: This is from the משנה in סנהדרין 45a.

phrases.english: was two people's height tall.
And it was taught about it: with his own height,
phrases.notes: "His own height" means the height of the person being pushed off.

phrases.english: there are three here.
And if it enters your mind
that there is a deadly impact in less than ten handbreadths,
why do I need all of this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: בֵּית הַסְּקִילָה הָיָה גָּבוֹהַּ שְׁתֵּי קוֹמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new attack on רב נחמן's view that impact can kill.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that a fall of under ten טפחים can kill
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a short fall can kill, the great height of the בית הסקילה would be unnecessary.

steps.title: Your view does not explain the height either
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן turns the question around: even רבא would agree that ten טפחים can kill, so why not build the platform only ten טפחים high?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, let us make it ten handbreadths!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן shows that רבא's proof does not hold up. רבא's own view cannot explain the height either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that a fall of ten טפחים can kill. So even for רבא, a platform two people high is far more than needed. This shows the height must have a different reason, which רב נחמן gives in the next step.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, let us make it ten handbreadths!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבא's challenge back on him.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the use of the platform's height as proof about ten טפחים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The height goes far beyond ten טפחים for everyone, so it cannot prove anything about short falls.

steps.title: The height gives a merciful death
steps.stepSummary: The real reason for the height is to give the condemned person a quick death, based on "וְאָהַבְתָּ לְרֵעֲךָ כָּמוֹךָ".
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it follows רב נחמן, who said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: the פסוק says "Love your fellow as yourself," so choose for him a good death.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the true reason for the tall platform. The Torah wants the condemned person to die quickly, without needless suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The height does not mark the lowest fall that can kill. It is set so death comes fast and gently. Because of this, the platform tells us nothing about whether a fall under ten טפחים can kill.

keyTerms.meaning: Choose for him a good, merciful death

steps.whatToRemember: The great height of the בית הסקילה exists to give a quick, merciful death (מיתה יפה). It does not show the minimum height needed to kill.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of מיתה יפה shows that the Torah requires compassion even for a person sentenced to death.
steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is quoting a teaching of his own, which he learned from רבה בר אבוה. It is not a different person with the same name.

phrases.english: Rather, it is like רב נחמן's teaching,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ,
phrases.english: for רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה:
The verse says: "And you shall love your fellow as yourself,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:18

phrases.english: choose for him a good death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the real reason for the height, which ends רבא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the height
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The height shows how far a person must fall for it to kill.
steps.terutzMaskana: The height is meant to give a quick, merciful death.

steps.title: Then make it even higher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the goal is a gentle death, why not raise the platform even more?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let us raise it even higher!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new reason. If more height means a quicker death, why stop at three people's height?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the platform's purpose is mercy, more height should mean more mercy. So the fixed limit needs an explanation.

phrases.english: If so, let us raise it more!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The מיתה יפה reason for the platform's height
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If height brings a quicker death, there should be no upper limit.

steps.title: Too high would disfigure him
steps.stepSummary: The platform is not made higher because a longer fall would badly disfigure the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he would become disfigured.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a higher fall would crush and disfigure the person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A merciful death also means a dignified one. Three people's height is high enough for a quick death but not so high that the body is mangled. Both parts of מיתה יפה set the height.
steps.whatToRemember: The height of the בית הסקילה balances two needs: a fast death, and not disfiguring the body.

phrases.english: Because he becomes disfigured.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: More height always means more mercy.
steps.terutzMaskana: Too much height disfigures the body, which is not a מיתה יפה.

steps.title: רבא quotes a teaching about roof railings
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא on the פסוק of מעקה. It teaches that the owner is liable only when someone falls off his roof, not onto it, and it describes both cases with a ten-טפחים difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected to רב נחמן: the פסוק says "if any man falls from it." "From it" means falling from the roof, not falling onto it. How so? If the public area was ten טפחים higher than the house and someone fell from the public area onto the house, the owner is exempt. If the public area was ten טפחים lower than the house and someone fell from the house into the public area, the owner is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is bringing a source to use against רב נחמן. This step only quotes the ברייתא; the actual challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the house owner is responsible only for falls from his roof. Both of its cases use a drop of ten טפחים. That number is the detail רבא is about to use against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him from a teaching
A railing around a roof, required by the תורה

phrases.english: He (רבא) raised an objection to him (רב נחמן):
"If any man falls from it";
phrases.notes: דברים 22:8. This is the פסוק about building a railing on your roof.

phrases.english: "From it": but not into it.
How so?
If the public domain was
ten handbreadths higher than it (the house),
and someone fell from it into it, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: Someone fell from the higher public area down onto the house.

phrases.english: If it was ten handbreadths lower than it,
and someone fell from it into it, he is liable.
phrases.notes: Now someone fell from the house's roof down into the public area.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the בית הסקילה discussion, רבא brings a new source against רב נחמן's view that a fall of less than ten טפחים can kill.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that a fall of less than ten טפחים can kill (יש חבטה בפחות מעשרה).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step sets up the source. The ברייתא uses ten טפחים as the height that requires a מעקה.

steps.title: Why does the railing law need ten handbreadths?
steps.stepSummary: If a fall of under ten טפחים can kill, why does the מעקה law require a ten-טפחים drop?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think a fall of less than ten טפחים is deadly, why do I need ten?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now makes his challenge from the ברייתא. If shorter falls can kill, the ten-טפחים rule makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A railing exists to keep people from falling to their death. If the תורה requires it only at ten טפחים, that suggests a shorter fall is not dangerous. That would go against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: A deadly impact from a fall

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that there is a deadly impact from less than ten (handbreadths),
why do I need ten?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ יֵשׁ חֲבָטָה בְּפָחוֹת מֵעֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ten-טפחים detail from the ברייתא in step 9 as the basis of the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that a fall of under ten טפחים can kill.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the תורה requires a railing only when the drop is ten טפחים, then smaller falls must not be deadly.

steps.title: A house must be ten handbreadths tall
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that ten טפחים is needed because anything shorter is not a בית, and only a בית needs a מעקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A house is different, because anything less than ten טפחים tall is not a house.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers that the ten טפחים have nothing to do with how dangerous a fall is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of מעקה applies only to a בית, and a building under ten טפחים tall is not a בית at all. So the ten-טפחים rule says what counts as a house. It does not prove that shorter falls are safe.

keyTerms.meaning: House; halachically it must be at least ten טפחים tall

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying the fall must be ten טפחים to be dangerous. He is saying the building must be ten טפחים tall to be a house at all.

phrases.english: He (רב נחמן) said to him:
A house is different,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכׇל פָּחוֹת מֵעֲשָׂרָה – לָאו בַּיִת הוּא.
phrases.english: since anything less than ten (handbreadths) is not a house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the reason for the number: it defines what counts as a house, not how dangerous the fall is.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ten טפחים in the ברייתא is the smallest fall that can kill.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ten טפחים is the smallest height for a building to count as a בית, which is required for the מעקה law.

steps.title: Inside, the house would be less than ten
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that if the house is ten טפחים from the outside, removing the ceiling and plaster leaves less than ten inside. By רב נחמן's rule it would not be a house.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then here too, where it is ten טפחים from the outside, take away the ceiling and the plaster: from the inside it is not ten!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's answer. The ברייתא's case does not seem to fit the rule that a house must be ten טפחים tall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא measures ten טפחים from the outside, from the ground to the roof. The ceiling and its plaster take up some of that height. So the room inside is less than ten טפחים tall, and by רב נחמן's own rule it should not count as a house.

keyTerms.meaning: From the outside / from the inside
A layer of plaster on top of the ceiling

phrases.english: If so,
now too, where it is ten (handbreadths) from the outside,
remove from it the ceiling and the plaster:
from the inside it is not ten!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי דְּהָוֵי מֵאַבָּרַאי עֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's answer from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that the ten טפחים is about whether the building counts as a house.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's ten-טפחים case, once you subtract the ceiling, gives a room less than ten tall. That would not be a house, so the ברייתא's ten cannot be explained this way.

steps.title: The floor was dug out inside
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the case is one where the owner dug out the floor inside, so the room is ten טפחים tall.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The case is where he dug out the inside.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his answer by explaining the exact case the ברייתא is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the floor was dug lower, the inside of the house reaches ten טפחים even with the ceiling's thickness. It is a true בית, so רב נחמן's view stands: a fall of less than ten טפחים can still kill.

keyTerms.meaning: For example; the case is where

steps.whatToRemember: For now, רב נחמן's answer is that the ten טפחים of מעקה is only the height a building needs to count as a בית, with the floor dug out inside. Step 14 knocks this down, and step 15 gives a different reason for רב נחמן's ruling.

phrases.english: He (רב נחמן) said to him:
It is a case where he dug out (the floor) inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case: the ברייתא is about a house whose floor was dug out.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ten טפחים measured from outside leaves less than ten inside.
steps.terutzMaskana: The floor was dug out, so the inside reaches ten טפחים and the building counts as a house.

steps.title: Digging could make almost any house ten inside
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that if digging the floor counts, a house that is not ten טפחים from the outside could still be ten טפחים inside. So the ברייתא's exemption for such a house makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even when the house is not ten טפחים from the outside, you can find a case where it is ten טפחים inside, for example if he dug out the floor more. So why should he be exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's last answer (step 13) by showing it proves too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a roof less than ten טפחים high from the outside needs no מעקה. If digging the floor can turn a room into a ten-טפחים בית, then even such a low house could be a בית inside. The 'not a בית' explanation for the ten-טפחים rule therefore collapses.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if you say this
He dug out (hollowed) more space in it

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לָא הָוֵי נָמֵי מֵאַבָּרַאי עֲשָׂרָה –
phrases.english: even when it is not ten from the outside,
you can find it being ten from the inside,
such as where he dug into it more!
phrases.notes: He means: dig the floor down far enough, and even a short house is ten טפחים tall inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, כִּי לָא הָוֵי נָמֵי מֵאַבָּרַאי עֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 13 by showing it undermines the ברייתא's exemption.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's answer that the house had a dug-out floor (step 13).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If digging makes a room a בית, then the outside height cannot decide whether it is a בית, so the ברייתא's exemption for a house under ten from the outside has no basis.

steps.title: The real reason: the ox's belly adds four טפחים
steps.stepSummary: The 'not a בית' explanation is dropped. רב נחמן's real reason is that the ox's belly is four טפחים above the ground. Added to the six-טפחים channel, the ox really falls ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is רב נחמן's reason. He holds: how far is it from an ox's belly to the ground? Four טפחים. How deep is the water channel? Six. That makes ten. So when the ox lands, it lands from a height of ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the whole earlier explanation and gives a new reason for רב נחמן's ruling about the ox in the water channel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רב נחמן no longer has to say that a fall under ten טפחים can kill. The ox lands on its belly, so the drop is measured from its belly: four טפחים of body plus six of channel equals ten. This fits the usual rule that ten טפחים is a deadly fall, so the מעקה question no longer bothers him.

keyTerms.meaning: A water channel used for irrigation

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's ruling rests on ten טפחים after all: four for the ox's body plus six for the channel.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַב נַחְמָן, סָבַר:
phrases.english: Rather, this is the reason of רב נחמן; he holds:
from the belly of the ox to the ground,
how much is it? Four.
The water channel, how deep is it? Six.
That makes ten.
It turns out that when it hits the ground,
it is from ten that it hits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 14 knocks out the 'not a בית' approach, this gives a new reason that keeps the ten-טפחים rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the underlying reason (drops the earlier approach)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן held that a fall of under ten טפחים can kill, which clashed with the מעקה rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ox really falls ten טפחים (four of its body plus six of the channel), so there is no clash with the ten-טפחים rule.

steps.title: Then why does the משנה require a ten-טפחים pit?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a pit able to kill is ten טפחים deep. If the ox's four-טפחים belly counts, a six-טפחים pit should already be deadly.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches: just as a pit deep enough to kill is ten טפחים, so too anything deep enough to kill is ten טפחים. According to this reasoning, six should also be enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reason from step 15, using the משנה about pits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an animal's own four טפחים of height are added to the drop, a pit only six deep already gives a ten-טפחים fall. Yet the משנה sets the deadly depth of a pit at ten טפחים, which seems to ignore the animal's height.

phrases.english: But the משנה, which teaches:

phrases.aramaic: מָה בּוֹר שֶׁהוּא כְּדֵי לְהָמִית – עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
phrases.english: just as a pit that can kill is ten טפחים,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית – עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים;
phrases.english: so too anything that can kill is ten טפחים.
Six should also be enough!
phrases.notes: Six טפחים of pit plus the animal's four טפחים already makes ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the new reason given in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the animal's belly height counts toward the ten טפחים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the animal's height counts, the משנה should have set a pit's deadly depth at six טפחים, not ten.

steps.title: The משנה is about an animal that rolled in
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's ten טפחים is for an animal that rolled into the pit. When it rolls in, its own height adds nothing, so the pit itself must be ten deep.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answered: the משנה is talking about an animal that rolled into the pit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from the משנה by limiting the משנה to a specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that rolls in falls lying down, so there is no extra drop from its belly, and the pit must be ten טפחים by itself. An animal that walks in and falls, like רב נחמן's ox, does add its four טפחים. The two rulings therefore do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: They said (an answer given without a named author)

steps.whatToRemember: Ten טפחים is always the deadly height. An animal that walks and falls counts its own four טפחים, but one that rolls in does not.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה and רב נחמן do not argue about how far a deadly fall is; both say ten. They only differ in whether the animal's height is part of the fall.

phrases.english: They said: the משנה is
where it rolled into the pit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 by limiting the משנה to a rolling animal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say a pit needs ten טפחים even for an animal that walks in and falls.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's ten טפחים is for an animal that rolled in. When an animal walks in and falls, its height counts.

steps.title: The second partner who leaves the shared pit uncovered is liable
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that when a pit belongs to two partners, and both passed it without covering it, the second partner is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A pit belongs to two partners. The first one walked past and did not cover it, and then the second one walked past and did not cover it. The second one is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It gives a ruling about a pit owned by two partners, where each one walked by and left it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both partners had a chance to cover the pit. The משנה puts the liability on the second one, the last person who could have covered it and did not.

keyTerms.meaning: A pit; one of the main categories of damage

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A pit belonging to two partners;
the first passed by it and did not cover it,
and the second, and did not cover it,
phrases.notes: The words 'passed by' are left out, but they're assumed: the second partner also walked past.

phrases.english: the second is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה. The previous discussion about how deep a deadly pit must be is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both partners pass a shared pit and leave it uncovered, the second one is liable.

steps.title: How can a pit belong to two partners?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what real case fits the משנה's 'pit of two partners'.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: They say: A pit belonging to two partners, how can such a case happen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the משנה's case could actually happen. This question sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא is not yet attacking the ruling. It wants to know what situation produces a pit that two partners are both responsible for.

keyTerms.meaning: They say; introduces an unnamed statement
How do you find it? How can this case happen?

phrases.english: GEMARA: They say:
A pit belonging to two partners,
how can you find it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בּוֹר שֶׁל שְׁנֵי שׁוּתָּפִין הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what case the משנה in step 18 is describing.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What real situation makes one pit belong to two partners?

steps.title: Under רבי עקיבא, a shared courtyard pit works
steps.stepSummary: Under רבי עקיבא, who holds a person liable for a pit on his own property, the case is two partners who made their shared courtyard ownerless but kept their shared pit.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well if we hold like רבי עקיבא, who says a pit on one's own property makes him liable. Then the case is a courtyard of both partners with a pit of both partners. They made their property ownerless but kept the pit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an easy answer, but only for רבי עקיבא's opinion. The partners made the shared courtyard ownerless and kept owning the pit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that an owner is liable for a pit on his own property even after he gives up the land. So two partners who share a courtyard and its pit are both responsible. The word הניחא, 'this works well', hints that the other opinion will be harder.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well; signals that a harder case is coming
We hold; we follow this opinion

phrases.aramaic: הָנִיחָא אִי סְבִירָא לַן כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: This works well if we hold like Rabbi Akiva,
who says: a pit in his own property, he is liable;
phrases.notes: He means someone who dug a pit on his land and then gave up the land but kept the pit.

phrases.english: you find it in a courtyard belonging to both of them
and a pit belonging to both of them,
and they made their property ownerless but did not make their pit ownerless.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא אִי סְבִירָא לַן כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19, but only under רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Under רבי עקיבא: a shared courtyard made ownerless, with the shared pit kept by both partners.

steps.title: Under the other view, a shared pit must be public, and that is hard to find
steps.stepSummary: If a pit on one's own property is exempt, liability only comes from a pit in רשות הרבים. How could two partners share a pit there?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if we hold that a pit on one's own property is exempt, where would someone be liable for a pit? Only in the public domain. And in the public domain, how can a pit belong to two partners?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the opposite opinion and shows that the easy answer no longer works. Now the pit has to be in a public place, which makes the question harder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this view the courtyard case gives no liability at all. Liability only exists for a pit in רשות הרבים. Nobody owns public ground, so the גמרא asks how two people could jointly 'own' a pit there.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt; does not have to pay

phrases.english: But if we hold
a pit in his own property is exempt;
how can you find a case where he is liable for it?
In the public domain,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים בּוֹר שֶׁל שְׁנֵי שׁוּתָּפִין
phrases.english: and in the public domain, a pit belonging to two partners
how can you find it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי סְבִירָא לַן בּוֹר בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that step 20's answer only works for רבי עקיבא. It raises the question again under the opposite view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of a shared pit, read according to those who exempt a pit on one's own property.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under this view liability only exists in רשות הרבים, and it is unclear how two people could jointly own a pit there.

steps.title: A shared agent who digs does not work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests both partners sent one agent to dig. It rejects this, because אין שליח לדבר עבירה: the agent alone is responsible.
steps.simpleTranslation: If both of them appointed an agent and told him, 'Go dig for us,' and he went and dug for them, that fails. There is no agency for doing something wrong!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests one way two partners could have a public pit: they sent a shared agent to dig. It knocks the idea down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Digging a pit in רשות הרבים is a wrongful act. In a wrongful act, the agent cannot pass his responsibility on to the people who sent him. So the agent who dug is liable, not the two partners, and it is not their shared pit.

keyTerms.meaning: Agent; someone who acts on another's behalf
There is no agency for doing something wrong; the one who acts is responsible

steps.confusionAlert: The partners are not liable even though they ordered the digging. In a wrongful act, the one who actually does it carries the responsibility.

phrases.english: If both of them appointed an agent,
and said to him: "Go dig for us,"
and he went and dug for them,
there is no agent for a matter of transgression!
phrases.notes: So the digger himself is responsible, and the pit does not count as the partners' pit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests one answer to step 21's question and rejects it right away.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the shared-agent scenario as a case of a pit belonging to two partners.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אין שליח לדבר עבירה: the responsibility stays with the agent who dug.

steps.title: Each partner digging five טפחים does not work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests each partner dug five טפחים. It rejects this, because the second partner's digging cancels the first partner's act.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if this one dug five and that one dug five, the first act has been removed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second way two partners could share a public pit: each one dug half. It rejects this one too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pit becomes deadly at ten טפחים, as the earlier steps showed. The second partner, who finished the pit to ten, made it a deadly pit. So the first partner's five טפחים no longer counts, and the pit is not truly shared.

keyTerms.meaning: Five; here five טפחים of depth
The first act; the first partner's digging

steps.whatToRemember: Under the view that a pit on one's own property is exempt, a shared agent fails because אין שליח לדבר עבירה. Splitting the digging fails, at least in most views, because the one who completes the ten טפחים carries the whole act. Step 24 notes one exception, and step 25 gives a case that works for everyone.

phrases.english: And if this one dug five
and that one five,
the first act has been removed!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי דִּכְרָה הַאי חַמְשָׁה וְהַאי חַמְשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the shared-agent idea fails in step 22, the גמרא tries a split-digging case and rejects it too.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the case where each partner digs five טפחים as a jointly owned pit.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The second digger, who brings the pit to ten טפחים, makes it deadly, so the first digger's act is set aside.

steps.title: Shared liability works only in one case, so how do we find the rest?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that under רבי a two-partner pit can exist for damages. It then asks how such a pit can exist for death under רבי, and for anything at all under the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to רבי for damages: there you can find a pit of two partners. But according to רבי for death, and according to the רבנן for both death and damages, how can you find such a case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that the 'five טפחים each' idea still works in one situation: רבי's view on damages. It then asks how the משנה's case can work everywhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rejection in step 23 (the second digger cancels the first) only holds in some views. רבי holds both diggers liable for damages, so partners are possible there. But for death under רבי, and for everything under the רבנן, only the last digger is liable, so we still need a real case of a shared pit.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (according to this view)
Damages / injuries caused by the pit
Death of the animal that fell in
How can you find (such a case)?

steps.confusionAlert: This step relies on a מחלוקת between רבי and the רבנן that the גמרא only quotes later, in step 27. Don't worry if it isn't clear yet why רבי treats damages differently; that comes soon.

phrases.english: It works well according to רבי, regarding damages,
phrases.notes: This means the 'five טפחים each' case from step 23 still works here.

phrases.english: you can find it.
But according to רבי regarding death,
and according to the רבנן, both for death and for damages,
how can you find it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבִּי – וְלִנְזָקִין, מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ. אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rejection of step 23 to some views and reopens the search for a case of a partners' pit.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of a pit belonging to two partners, under רבי for death and under the רבנן entirely
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the second digger cancels the first, only one person is ever liable, so no shared pit is possible in those views.

steps.title: Both partners removed the last piece of earth together
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the two partners pulled out the final piece of earth at the same moment and so finished the pit to ten טפחים together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: For example, both of them pulled out a clump of earth at the same time and finished the pit to ten טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a case that works for every view: the partners finished the pit together, at one moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that one digger's act always replaces the other's. If both dig out the last clump at the very same instant, neither came 'after' the other. So both made the pit reach ten טפחים, and both are liable, even for death and even under the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A clump or piece of earth
Completed it to ten (טפחים), the depth that can kill

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן said:
For example, where both of them pulled out a clump of earth
at the same time,
and completed it to ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כְּגוֹן שֶׁעָקְרוּ שְׁנֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24 with a case that works for all views.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every way of two people digging seemed to leave only one person liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: When both complete the pit at the same instant, neither cancels the other, so both share liability.

steps.title: What exactly do רבי and the רבנן hold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the מחלוקת between רבי and the רבנן that it has been relying on.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי's view and what is the רבנן's view?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask where this מחלוקת comes from. This sets up the ברייתא it is about to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 used an argument between רבי and the רבנן without quoting it. Now the גמרא asks to see it so we understand the background.

phrases.english: What is the view of רבי, and what is the view of the רבנן?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the opinions mentioned in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source text of the מחלוקת between רבי and the רבנן

steps.title: The ברייתא: one digs nine, another finishes to ten
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that if one person dug nine טפחים and another finished to ten, the רבנן hold only the last digger liable. רבי holds the last one liable for death, but both liable for damages.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: If one person digs a pit nine טפחים deep, and another comes and finishes it to ten, the last one is liable. רבי says: For death, we go after the last one. For damages, we go after both of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that contains the מחלוקת between רבי and the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן put all the blame on whoever finished the pit. רבי splits it: only a ten-טפחים pit can kill, so the last digger alone pays for death. But the nine-טפחים pit was already able to injure, so both diggers share the payment for damages.

keyTerms.meaning: We go after both of them (both pay)

steps.whatToRemember: רבנן: the last digger alone is liable for everything. רבי: the last digger alone for death, both diggers for damages.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
One who digs a pit nine (טפחים deep),
and another came and completed it to ten,
the last one is liable.
רבי says: We go after the last one for death,
and after both of them for damages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26 by quoting the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבנן: only the finisher is liable. רבי: the finisher alone for death, both diggers for damages.

steps.title: Why do the רבנן blame only the last digger?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the רבנן's view that only the last digger is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the רבנן ignore the first digger completely. This sets up the source from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems unfair that the first person, who dug most of the pit, pays nothing. The גמרא wants to know what source forces the רבנן's view.

phrases.english: What is the reason of the רבנן?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the רבנן's ruling in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the פסוק for the רבנן's view

steps.title: The extra word 'יכרה' teaches that the second digger cancels the first
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says both 'כי יפתח' (if he opens) and 'כי יכרה' (if he digs). Since digging is obviously included if opening is, the extra word teaches the case of one digger after another: the second removes the first one's act.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the פסוק says: 'If a man opens' and 'if a man digs.' If he is liable for opening, isn't it obvious that he is liable for digging? Rather, it comes to include a digger after a digger, where the second removed the act of the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the word 'יכרה' would be unnecessary. So it is read as teaching the case of a second digger, who takes over full responsibility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Opening an existing pit is a small act, and it already makes a person liable. So digging a whole pit obviously makes him liable too, and 'יכרה' seems extra. The extra word teaches that someone who digs after another person counts as the digger of the whole pit, and the first person's work no longer counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it all the more so? (it is obvious)

steps.whatToRemember: This is the גמרא's first suggestion for the רבנן's source. It does not last: step 31 knocks it down, and step 32 gives the real source, the singular word 'איש'.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that the later digger replaces the earlier one explains the rejection in step 23 and why רבי יוחנן needed a case where both partners dig at the same instant. The source for that rule, however, will change in step 32.

phrases.english: Because the פסוק says:
'If he opens' and 'if he digs':
phrases.notes: שמות 21:33

phrases.english: if he is liable for opening,
for digging, isn't it all the more so?
Rather, it comes to include one digging after another digger,
where he removed the act of the first.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר קְרָא: כִּי יִפְתַּח וְכִי יִכְרֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28 with a reading of the extra word in the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word 'יכרה' includes a second digger, whose act cancels the first digger's act.

steps.title: רבי says both words in the פסוק are already needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי explains why he does not learn the רבנן's rule from 'כי יפתח' and 'כי יכרה': both words are needed for other lessons.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי would tell you: those two words are both needed, as we said earlier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי would respond to the source just given for the רבנן. He would say both words are needed for something else, so neither is extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 treated 'כי יכרה' as an extra word that teaches 'the second digger removes the first one's act.' רבי answers that both 'opening' and 'digging' were already used for other lessons earlier (on 50a). So for him, nothing is left over to teach this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: They are needed (each word has its own lesson)
He would say to you (how a side would respond)

phrases.english: And רבי would say to you:
those two words are both needed,
as we said.
phrases.notes: This points back to 50a, where each word in the פסוק was already given its own lesson.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי avoids the derivation the רבנן used in step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both words of the פסוק are already needed elsewhere
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word 'כי יכרה' is extra and teaches that the second digger removes the first one's act.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי, neither word is extra, so he does not learn this rule from them.

steps.title: The רבנן also need both words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the רבנן also need both words for those same lessons, so where do they get their rule?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the רבנן also need both words!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns רבי's point against the רבנן. If the two words are needed for other lessons, the רבנן need them too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lessons from 50a are not part of the argument between רבי and the רבנן, so both sides use those words the same way. That means the source in step 29 cannot work for the רבנן either. Their view now needs a new source.

phrases.english: And the רבנן also need them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי's point from step 30 to knock down the source given for the רבנן in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The source for the רבנן given in step 29 (the extra word 'כי יכרה').
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both words are needed for other lessons, they are not extra for the רבנן either, so the רבנן have no source.

steps.title: A new source for the רבנן: 'a man' means one person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the earlier source. The רבנן learn from 'איש' (a man) in the פסוק: one person is liable, not two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is the reason of the רבנן: the פסוק says 'If a man shall dig a pit.' One person, and not two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a brand-new reason for the רבנן's view that only the last digger is liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'איש' (a man) is singular. So only one person can be held liable for a בור, not two partners. When two people dug in stages, the one who finished it to ten טפחים is the liable one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the real source for the רבנן's ruling that only the one who finishes the pit to ten טפחים pays.

phrases.english: Rather, this is the reason of the רבנן:
the verse says: 'If a man shall dig a pit',
phrases.notes: שמות 21:33

phrases.english: one, and not two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source that was knocked down in step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source from the singular word 'איש'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן learned their rule from the extra word 'כי יכרה'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן learn it from 'איש': one person is liable, not two.

steps.title: רבי uses 'a man' to exclude an ox that digs
steps.stepSummary: רבי does not learn 'one, not two' from 'איש', because he needs it to teach that a man is liable for digging a pit, but not if his ox dug it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי? He needs that phrase: 'If a man shall dig a pit' teaches a man, and not an ox that digs a pit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי does not accept the רבנן's source, and answers that he needs the word 'איש' for a different lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, the word 'איש' teaches who must do the digging: a person, not an animal. If someone's ox dug a pit, the owner is not liable for it as a בור. Since the word is used up for that lesson, רבי cannot also learn 'one and not two' from it.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox that digs a pit

phrases.english: And רבי? He needs that phrase:

phrases.aramaic: ״כִּי יִכְרֶה אִישׁ בּוֹר״ – וְלֹא שׁוֹר בּוֹר.
phrases.english: 'If a man shall dig a pit': and not an ox that digs a pit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי does not accept the new source for the רבנן from step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The word is needed for a different lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'איש' must teach 'one and not two', which would make רבי's view hard to explain.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי, 'איש' teaches 'a man and not an ox', so it cannot also teach 'one and not two'.

steps.title: The רבנן: 'man… pit' is written twice
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן can learn both lessons, because the words 'איש בור' appear twice in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? 'A man… a pit' is written twice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the רבנן also get the lesson 'a man and not an ox': the words 'man' and 'pit' appear twice, so each one teaches a different lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'כי יפתח איש בור או כי יכרה איש בור'. The רבנן use one 'איש בור' for 'a man and not an ox' and the other for 'one and not two'. רבי does not use the second one this way, so he holds both diggers liable for damages.
steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן: the singular 'איש' teaches that only one person is liable, so only the last digger pays. רבי: 'איש' only teaches 'a man and not an ox', so both diggers share liability for damages.

phrases.english: And the רבנן? 'A man… a pit' is written twice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the רבנן cover the lesson רבי learned in step 33 and still keep their own source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The phrase appears twice, so there are two lessons
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן would have no source for 'a man and not an ox' if 'איש' teaches 'one and not two'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase is written twice: one teaches 'not an ox', the other teaches 'one and not two'.

steps.title: Why רבי is not bothered by the doubled words
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds that the second 'איש בור' teaches nothing new. The Torah simply repeated the same style it used in the first clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי? Since the Torah wrote this phrase once, it wrote it again the same way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: if the רבנן use the doubled 'איש בור' to learn two lessons, what does רבי do with the repetition? He says it is only the Torah's way of phrasing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 34 the רבנן used the repeated words to get both 'one, not two' and 'a man, not an ox'. רבי does not accept the extra lesson, because to him the second mention just copies the wording of the first. So he has only one lesson from 'איש', the ox lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it wrote this, it wrote that: the second phrase only follows the style of the first and teaches nothing new
רבי יהודה הנשיא, who argues with the רבנן here

phrases.english: And Rabbi [what does he do with the repeated words]?
phrases.notes: The גמרא skips the question itself: how does רבי explain the doubled 'איש בור' from Step 34?

phrases.english: Since it wrote this,
it wrote this.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי – אַיְּידֵי דִּכְתַב הַאי, כְּתַב הַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the exchange from Step 34 by giving רבי's side: he reads the repetition as a matter of style.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The repeated wording is explained as style, not an extra teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the words 'איש בור' appear twice, רבי should also learn two lessons from them.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי sees the second mention as copying the first, so he learns only one lesson from 'איש'.

steps.title: Maybe the first digger is the liable one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the רבנן: even if only one digger is liable, why say it is the last one? Maybe it is the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know the Torah means to make the last one liable? Maybe it means to make the first one liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the רבנן. Their source shows that only one person pays, but it does not say which one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'איש' tells us 'one, not two', but both diggers are equally 'a man who dug'. The first one dug most of the pit, so you might think he should be the liable one. The רבנן need a reason to pick the last digger.

keyTerms.meaning: The last one: the digger who finished the pit
The first one: the digger who started the pit
Perhaps; used to suggest a different possibility

phrases.english: And from where [do we know] that it is to make the last one liable?
phrases.notes: The last one is the person who took the pit from nine טפחים to ten.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is to make the first one liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמַּאי דִּלְחַיּוֹבֵי בָּתְרָא? דִּלְמָא לְחַיּוֹבֵי קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the רבנן's source from 'איש' but asks which of the two diggers it points to.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's ruling that the last digger alone is liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'One, not two' does not say which one, and the first digger seems just as fitting, or even more fitting.

steps.title: The one who caused the death is liable
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'והמת יהיה לו' shows the Torah is speaking about the digger who made the pit deadly, and that is the last one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that, because the פסוק says 'And the dead one shall be his': that means the one who causes the death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the Torah points to the last digger, because the פסוק links liability to whoever caused the animal's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pit of nine טפחים is not deep enough to kill. The tenth טפח made it deadly, so the person who added it is the one who 'causes the death'. That is why the רבנן place the liability on the last digger.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't even think that; this rejects the suggestion
And the dead one shall be his (שמות 21:34)

phrases.english: It should not enter your mind,
since the verse says: "And the dead one shall be his"
phrases.notes: שמות 21:34

phrases.english: [meaning] the one who causes the death.
phrases.notes: The tenth טפח is what makes the pit deep enough to kill, so this is the last digger.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״וְהַמֵּת יִהְיֶה לוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 36 by bringing a second פסוק that identifies which digger is liable.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new פסוק is brought to identify which person is liable
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first digger, who started the pit, might be the liable one.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'והמת יהיה לו' points to the one who caused the death, and that is the last digger.

steps.title: That פסוק is needed for רבא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that 'והמת יהיה לו' is already used by רבא to exempt a pit owner when a disqualified קדשים ox falls in. So the פסוק seems unavailable for the 'last digger' lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this 'And the dead one shall be his' is needed for רבא's teaching. רבא said: if an ox of disqualified consecrated animals fell into a pit, the pit owner is exempt, because it says 'And the dead one shall be his', meaning a case where the dead animal belongs to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 37. The same words are already used for a different lesson by רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads 'והמת יהיה לו' as a condition: the pit owner pays only when the dead animal's owner fully owns the carcass. With an ox of פסולי המוקדשין, the carcass is not fully his, so the pit owner is exempt. If the פסוק is busy teaching that, it seems it cannot also teach which digger is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for: the words are already used for another lesson
Consecrated animals that became unfit for a קרבן
Exempt; does not have to pay
An אמורא whose ruling is quoted here

phrases.english: But this "And the dead one shall be his"
is needed for that which Rava [teaches],
as Rava said:
An ox of disqualified consecrated animals
phrases.notes: An animal set aside for a קרבן that became unfit, so it's no longer fully the owner's ordinary property.

phrases.english: that fell into a pit: [the pit owner is] exempt,
as it is said: "And the dead one shall be his"
[the verse speaks] of one whose dead animal is his!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי ״וְהַמֵּת יִהְיֶה לוֹ״ מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 37 by showing that its פסוק is already used for רבא's lesson.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of 'והמת יהיה לו' to show that the last digger is liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק is normally used for one lesson. רבא already uses these words to exempt a pit owner when the ox is פסולי המוקדשין, so they seem unavailable for the רבנן's lesson.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא's case has nothing to do with two diggers. It is brought only to show that the same words already teach something else.

steps.title: The verse itself shows it is speaking about the one who caused death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that even though רבא uses 'והמת יהיה לו' for his own lesson, the context of the פסוק already shows it is talking about the digger who caused the death.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answered: Don't you already understand on your own that we are dealing with the one who caused the death?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 38. Even if רבא uses the words 'והמת יהיה לו' for his lesson, we still know the פסוק is about the digger who made the pit deadly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that the פסוק was already 'used up' by רבא, so it could not also teach the 'last digger' rule. The answer is that the 'last digger' lesson does not need a separate word. Since the פסוק talks about an animal dying, it is plainly speaking about the person whose digging caused that death, and that is the one who finished the deadly depth. So the same פסוק works for both lessons.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'last digger' rule comes from the context of the פסוק, which speaks about causing death. So it does not compete with רבא's use of 'והמת יהיה לו.'

phrases.english: They said: And is it not by itself
phrases.notes: This is a question that really means 'Of course you can already tell.'

phrases.english: that you learn from it,
that we are dealing with the one who caused death?
phrases.notes: In this case that is the last digger, whose digging made the pit deep enough to kill.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 38 that the פסוק was already used by רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The lesson comes from the plain context of the פסוק, not from extra words, so the פסוק can serve both lessons.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'last digger' lesson needed the words 'והמת יהיה לו' all to itself, and רבא had already used them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The context of the פסוק already shows it means the one who caused the death, so both lessons stand.

steps.title: Three diggers each add ten handbreadths: all are liable
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if one person digs a pit ten טפחים deep, another deepens it to twenty, and another to thirty, all of them are liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If one person digs a pit ten handbreadths deep, then another comes and deepens it to twenty, and another comes and deepens it to thirty, all of them are liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about several people who dig the same pit in turns. Its ruling is that all of them are liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten טפחים is already a deadly depth, so the first digger made a dangerous pit. The second and third diggers made it deeper still, and each one is held liable. This ruling sets up the contradiction in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֶחָד הַחוֹפֵר בּוֹר עֲשָׂרָה,
phrases.english: The Sages taught: One who digs a pit of ten,
and another came and completed it to twenty,
and another came and completed it to thirty –
they are all liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֶחָד הַחוֹפֵר בּוֹר עֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related discussion about several people working on one pit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When three people each dig another ten טפחים of the same pit, all three are liable.

steps.title: A second ברייתא says only the one who plastered is liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets against the first ברייתא another one: if one person digs ten טפחים and another plasters and cements the pit, only the last one is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they contrasted it with another teaching: If one person digs a pit ten handbreadths deep, and another comes and plasters and cements it, the last one is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a second ברייתא that seems to clash with the first one. The answer to this contradiction comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first ברייתא, the first digger stays liable even after others worked on the pit. Here the first digger made a ten-טפחים pit, but once someone else plastered and cemented it, only the last person is liable. The two rulings seem to point in opposite directions about the first person.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted it (raised a contradiction)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. In the first, each person digs deeper. In the second, the later person only plasters and cements, and does not dig deeper.

phrases.english: And they contrasted it: One who digs a pit of ten,
and another came and plastered and cemented it –
the last one is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהוּ: אֶחָד הַחוֹפֵר בּוֹר עֲשָׂרָה, וּבָא אַחֵר וְסִיֵּיד וְכִיֵּיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a contradiction against the ברייתא in step 40.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in step 40 that all the diggers, including the first, are liable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the second ברייתא, a later person's work on a ten-טפחים pit makes only the last person liable. So why does the first digger stay liable in the first ברייתא?
